The attack began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to execution of a malicious DLL via rundll32.exe from the user's Temp directory. Although the sandbox classified payloads as clean, behavioral analysis confirmed malicious activity including execution from Outlook, unsigned DLL loading, and beaconing to known-bad infrastructure. Containment actions were denied due to policy and parameter errors.

        description = "Detects executables in Linux cron directories with hidden or non-standard names"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        date = "2026-04-31"
    strings:
        $s1 = "/var/spool/cron/" nocase
        $s2 = "/etc/cron.d/" nocase
        $s3 = ".job" fullword ascii
        $s4 = ".tmp" fullword ascii
        $s5 = "libproc" fullword ascii
    condition:
        ( $s1 or $s2 ) and ( $s3 or $s4 or $s5 )
}

arguments.summary: An advanced persistent threat (APT-29) leveraged an initial foothold via a compromised engineering workstation (WS-ENG-015) to conduct internal reconnaissance and lateral movement toward build servers. The threat actor used encrypted C2 channels (Cobalt Strike beacon) from multiple hosts, evading existing detection rules. Despite EDR and SIEM coverage, critical Sigma rules (SIGMA-LAT-004, SIGMA-CRED-012, SIGMA-C2-007) failed to trigger. Administrative containment actions were denied, highlighting policy or approval bottlenecks.

timeline.description: External IP 203.0.113.88 conducted Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged but not blocked.
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk.
Host WS-FIN-042 established outbound HTTPS connection to 198.51.100.23 (unclassified IP).
Suspicious rundll32 execution detected on WS-FIN-042 from Temp directory.
IDS alert: Cobalt Strike beacon C2 communication detected from WS-FIN-042 to 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicative of credential misuse or pass-the-ticket attempt.
Lateral movement confirmed via SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server WS-FIN-050.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine) attempted but denied due to policy restrictions.

arguments.summary: An APT-29 campaign initiated from external C2 IP 203.0.113.88 conducted reconnaissance via port scanning against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Initial access was likely achieved through credential compromise or lateral movement, with suspicious activity observed on engineering workstations WS-ENG-015 and SRV-BUILD-01. Chrome.exe on SRV-BUILD-01 established persistent outbound connections to external IPs. No malicious payloads were confirmed via sandboxing, but detection gaps were identified in encrypted C2 monitoring and credential-based attack rules.

Incident escalated after correlation of scan activity, lateral movement patterns, and anomalous browser-based C2 behavior.
